chain_sync_status.description: Liveness record for OGCR-chain-cache: one record per chain, rewritten at the end of every mirror run. The other *_on_chain entities say what is on the chain; this says when anything last looked. Without it a quiet chain is indistinguishable from a dead mirror, because the newest mint could be old for either reason. Consumers should treat a record older than a few multiples of interval_seconds as stale.

sync_key.description: Business key: "chain-<chain_id>". One record per chain, overwritten each run. A string key so it can be matched with a server-side query filter.

chain_id.description: EVM chain id that was read.

head_block.description: Chain head at the end of the run. Rising across runs is the clearest sign the chain itself is alive, as opposed to only the mirror.

synced_at.description: UTC RFC-3339 timestamp of when the run finished. This is the field a heartbeat is actually built on.

run_status.description: "ok" when every configured mirror completed with no errors, "partial" when the chain was reachable but some records failed to write. A run that cannot reach the chain at all writes nothing, so the previous record simply ages.

mirrored_types.description: Which mirrors ran, comma separated. Distinguishes a count of zero meaning "none found" from a mirror that was skipped because its contract is not configured.

interval_seconds.description: Expected seconds between runs, from SYNC_INTERVAL_SECONDS. 0 when the cacher was run by hand. Lets a consumer decide what counts as stale without hardcoding the schedule.

error_count.description: Records that failed to upsert during the run.

parcel_count.description: Parcel tokens mirrored in this run.

activity_count.description: Activity tokens mirrored in this run.

certification_count.description: Certification tokens mirrored in this run.

credit_batch_count.description: Carbon credit batch tokens mirrored in this run.

credit_balance_count.description: Carbon credit holder balances mirrored in this run.
